screens.title: Spot the problem
screens.text: The root of this tree has a balance factor of 0, because its left and right branches have the same height. Is every node balanced?
screens.reveal: No. Nodes 30 and 70 each have one branch that is two levels taller than the other. Checking only the root is not enough.

screens.title: Goal
screens.text: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to calculate heights and balance factors and decide whether a tree is an AVL tree.

task.stem: What is the height of a leaf?
task.hint: This question checks heights and balance factors. Height counts the edges down to a leaf, and the balance factor is h(right) − h(left), where an empty branch counts as −1.

options.explanation: That counts the leaf itself as a node. Height counts edges, so a leaf has height 0.
A leaf has no edges below it, so its height is 0.
−1 is the height of an empty branch, which is one level below a leaf.

screens.title: Height
screens.text: The height of a node is the number of edges on the longest path from that node down to a leaf. A leaf has height 0. An empty branch has height −1, which is one less than a leaf.
screens.caption: 10, 30 and 50 are leaves, so they have height 0. Node 40 has height 1, and the root, 20, has height 2.

screens.title: Balance factor
screens.text: The balance factor (bf) of a node is the height of its right branch minus the height of its left branch, bf = h(right) − h(left).
points: A positive balance factor means that the right branch is taller.
A negative balance factor means that the left branch is taller.
A balance factor of 0 means that both branches have the same height.
Node 20 has a right branch of height 1 and a left branch of height 0, so its balance factor is 1 − 0 = +1.
Node 10 is a leaf. Both of its branches are empty, with height −1, so its balance factor is −1 − (−1) = 0.
screens.showRule: The balance factor is the height of the right branch minus the height of the left branch. An empty branch has height −1.

screens.title: The AVL rule
points: In an AVL tree, every node has a balance factor of −1, 0 or +1.
The rule applies at every node, not just the root. Every subtree of an AVL tree is itself an AVL tree.
The tree does not have to be perfectly balanced, because a difference of 1 is allowed.
Each node stores its height, so balance factors are quick to recompute.
The height of an AVL tree is at most roughly 1.44 log(n + 2) − 1.328, and in practice it is only slightly more than log n. This is stated here without proof.
screens.showRule: An AVL tree is a BST in which every node has a balance factor of −1, 0 or +1.

screens.title: Worked example: from the leaves up
screens.text: Work from the leaves up, because the height of a node depends on the heights of its children.
steps: Node 5 is a leaf. Both of its branches are empty, with height −1, so its balance factor is −1 − (−1) = 0.
Node 10 has an empty right branch (height −1) and a left branch of height 0, so its balance factor is −1 − 0 = −1.
Node 25 is a leaf. Both of its branches are empty, with height −1, so its balance factor is −1 − (−1) = 0.
Node 20 has a right branch of height 0 and a left branch of height 1, so its balance factor is 0 − 1 = −1.
Node 50 is a leaf. Both of its branches are empty, with height −1, so its balance factor is −1 − (−1) = 0.
Node 40 has a right branch of height 0 and an empty left branch (height −1), so its balance factor is 0 − (−1) = +1.
Node 30 has a right branch of height 1 and a left branch of height 2, so its balance factor is 1 − 2 = −1.
Every balance factor is −1, 0 or +1, so this is an AVL tree, even though its levels are not full.

screens.title: Balanced does not mean full
screens.caption: The tree on the left is an AVL tree, although its levels are not full. The tree on the right is not an AVL tree, because node 7 has a balance factor of −2. These are the two trees in Figure 4.29 of the textbook.
screens.text: Requiring equal heights at every node would be too rigid, because only perfect trees with 2ᵏ − 1 nodes would pass. The AVL rule allows a difference of 1 and still keeps the height O(log n).

screens.title: Lesson check
screens.text: This check has one question for each assessment criterion of the lesson's objective. You can re-attempt each question once, and the Hint button is always available.

screens.title: Summary
points: Height counts edges. A leaf has height 0, and an empty branch has height −1.
The balance factor is h(right) − h(left), so a negative value means that the left branch is taller.
Under the AVL rule, every node has a balance factor of −1, 0 or +1, not only the root.
